item.title: Upper Trapezius Positional Release
clinicalUse: Painful neck movement where comfort positioning improves the comparable sign
patientPosition: Supine or supported sitting with head and arm supported.
therapistPosition: At head/side of table so shoulder and neck can be positioned without patient effort.
stabilization: Support head and affected arm fully.
contact: One light monitoring finger over the tender point; avoid strong sustained pressure.
forceDirection: Move shoulder/head toward the position of maximal comfort and tissue shortening rather than stretch.
dosage: Hold comfortable position about 60–90 seconds or until tenderness clearly settles, then return slowly.
safety: Avoid positions that provoke dizziness, neurological symptoms or violate medical precautions.
item.visualCue: Tender point monitored lightly → position toward ease → hold → slow return → re-test.

subTechniques.name: Upper Trapezius Tender Point — Positional Release
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Reduce tenderness and protective guarding before active neck/shoulder movement.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine or supported sitting. Elevate the shoulder slightly and fine-tune cervical side-bending/rotation toward the position that reduces tenderness by roughly 70% or more.
subTechniques.contact: Maintain a light monitoring contact over the tender point; do not press harder during the hold.
subTechniques.direction: Hold the position of maximal comfort without stretching. Make very small adjustments if tenderness begins to return.
subTechniques.dosage: Usually about 60–90 seconds, then return slowly to neutral.
subTechniques.reassess: Tenderness, cervical side-bending/rotation and shoulder-elevation comfort.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: The treatment is guided by the drop in tenderness, not by forcing a memorized angle.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Return to neutral slowly; sudden repositioning can reproduce guarding.

subTechniques.name: Levator Scapulae Tender Point — Positional Release
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Reduce focal tenderness and guarding associated with painful neck rotation or scapular elevation.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supported sitting or supine. Elevate the shoulder and position the neck through small flexion/rotation/side-bending changes until the tender point becomes markedly more comfortable.
subTechniques.contact: Lightly monitor the superior-medial scapular/levator tender point while supporting the head and shoulder.
subTechniques.direction: Maintain the position of ease; do not add a stretch during the hold.
subTechniques.dosage: 60–90 seconds followed by a slow return to neutral.
subTechniques.reassess: Local tenderness, neck rotation and functional shoulder movement.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: If tenderness does not clearly reduce in the setup, abandon that position instead of holding it by habit.
